title: Audit provenance model and compact diff payloads for admin actions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Define a compact, provenance-aware audit event envelope and delta encoding for RBAC v2 admin operations (create/update/delete role bindings, policy changes, SSO config changes) that: 1) preserves developer-friendly, queryable fields (actor, target, action, request_id, timestamps), 2) includes strong provenance (who staged vs executed, source: console/api/automation, SAML/SSO assertion id, session_id), 3) encodes state diffs as a compact, typed op list to minimize storage and bandwidth while preserving fidelity for replay/forensics, and 4) supports configurable redaction/sampling and backward-compatible versioning.
acceptance_criteria: A1: New audit envelope spec document published in Confluence with example events for role create/update/delete and SSO config changes.
A2: Server-side encoder produces compact diff op lists for policy changes that are <= 40% the size of naive JSON before/after snapshots for standard change sizes in our traffic sample.
A3: Audit events include provenance fields (staged_by, executed_by, source, saml_assertion_id, session_id) for all admin paths with existing RBAC v2 API coverage.
A4: Queryability: Console and Console-API tools can filter by actor, action, target.type, target.id, and request_id; diffs are expandable on demand for full context.
A5: Security review signoff on redaction rules and sampling policy (PII thresholds) from Security team.
A6: Backfill plan documented: how to migrate existing events to envelope.v2 minimally and mapping for stored snapshots.
decisions: D1: Use an event envelope with 'schema_version' (string) and 'event_type' and separate 'payload' that contains the compact diff or snapshot reference.

D2: Diff encoding will be an array of typed ops: each op is serialized as a compact string token of the form '<OP>|<JSON-Pointer>|<TYPE>|<VALUE>' where OP ∈ {SET, UNSET, PATCH, INSERT, REMOVE} and TYPE is a lightweight indicator (s = string, n = number, b = bool, j = json, h = hash). This keeps events flat and line-delimited in storage indexes.

D3: Provenance model will include both staging context and execution context: staged_by, staged_request_id, executed_by, executed_request_id, source_type (console | api | automation), saml_assertion_id, session_id, justification (optional), and impersonation boolean.

D4: PII and large blobs are not stored in plaintext: values above a size threshold or flagged by schema will be replaced with a hash token using SHA256 and an optional archival_ref to a redacted store (access-controlled).
D5: Default retention for detailed diffs is 365 days; configurable per-org retention overrides in Dedicated/Private plans.
D6: Provide a helper library (go/ts) to encode/decode the compact ops and to expand an op list into a hydrated JSON patch for audit replay tools.
D7: Sampling: low-risk reads/updates can be sampled; high-risk admin actions (role changes, SAML config, key rotation) are always logged in full (subject to redaction rules).
D8: Backwards compatibility: existing events with full snapshots will be preserved; new events will use envelope.v2. Event routers will support both formats until deprecation window.
examples:
Example: human-readable envelope.v2 (multiline for clarity):
{
  "schema_version": "v2.0",
  "event_id": "evt_20250214_9f2a",
  "timestamp": "2025-02-14T18:12:03Z",
  "event_type": "rbac.role_binding.update",
  "actor": {"id": "user_128", "type": "user", "email_hash": "h:7b9..."},
  "target": {"type": "role_binding", "id": "rb-53"},
  "provenance": {"staged_by": "user_128", "staged_request_id": "req_aa12", "executed_by": "automation_deploy", "executed_request_id": "req_bb34", "source_type": "automation", "saml_assertion_id": "saml_982ef", "session_id": "sess_11", "impersonation": "false"},
  "payload_type": "compact-diff",
  "payload": [
    "SET|/bindings/1/role|s|team-admin",
    "UNSET|/bindings/1/conditions|j|\"\"",
    "SET|/bindings/1/metadata/modified_by|s|user_128"
  ]
}

This example uses op tokens to keep the event compact and indexable. The console UI will expand the payload into a JSON patch view on-demand.
Example: compact binary-safe op for large value redaction: 'SET|/sso/sso_cert|h|sha256:ab12...|archival_ref:store://audit/arch/20250214/evt_9f2a' — shows hashing + archival pointer.
notes: Implementation plan: 1) Write envelope.v2 spec in Confluence and circulate to Security/Compliance. 2) Implement encoder/decoder library in Go (core server) and TypeScript (console). 3) Add server-side middleware to produce provenance fields for all admin endpoints (staging + execution separation). 4) Integrate redaction and archival hooks; add unit tests for sampled vs forced logging. 5) Update ingestion pipeline and dashboards to support compact op lists and expansion on demand.

Trade-offs: compact ops reduce storage and network but make ad-hoc querying of field values slower unless we build specialized inverted indices for common query paths (actor, target, action). Consider maintaining a small set of denormalized columns for hot queries.
Performance target: end-to-end event encode latency < 5ms on hot path for API calls; batch archival operation will be async to avoid blocking commits.

Compatibility: will provide an adapter that converts existing snapshot events into a single 'SET' op list entry for compatibility views; do not rewrite historical rows by default to avoid heavy IO during rollout.

Observability: create a Grafana dashboard showing average event size by path, ratio of hashed values, and ops-per-event distribution. Key metric: percent of events with provenance.staged_by != provenance.executed_by (indicates automation vs human staging).
